Team — forwarding FinAdvisor's note. Quick read: they hit a few multi-minute sustained bursts that pushed them ~38% over their reserved commit for a 24h window. They attached token-level export. Key asks: metering calculation, throttle semantics, and short-term remedial options (credits or temp burst).

Proposed internal approach:
1) Confirm metering: we bill per-token processed to the Dedicated pool; aggregation window is 60s with continuous batching applied.
2) Throttle: auto-throttle triggers when sustained 5-minute moving-average > 1.5x committed throughput on that pool for > 10 minutes. Throttle is soft: we reduce concurrency then fall back to hosted model variants if configured.
3) Short-term remedy: offer a one-time invoice credit equal to the first 12 hours of above-commit spend if they convert to a 12-month reserved commit increase (50% incremental commit).

I think we can do better on the wording. Aditya, can you confirm the exact metering window and whether the throttle fallback path they see would send them to hosted API (and the cost delta)? Camila/Laura, want a pricing sentence we can send that is simple and customer-facing.

-Markus

Markus,

Confirmed details from the runtime team and billing:
- Metering: tokens are metered at the inference layer post-batching. We use a rolling 60s aggregation to convert per-request token counts into the pool-level consumption metric. That means very short microspikes are absorbed by batching; sustained bursts (multi-minute) are what create above-commit billing events.
- Throttle behavior: soft-throttle engages when the 5-min moving average exceeds 150% of committed throughput for > 10 minutes. The runtime lowers new request admission and increases queuing; customers see increased latency. If configured, requests can be routed to a hosted fallback model (higher per-token rate) to avoid request failures.
- Billing math: above-commit tokens are billed at committed rate + 25% surcharge and are reported on the next invoice cycle. There is also a monthly true-up that consolidates burst charges.

I also attached a short example calculation (see proposed_pricing_v2.pdf) showing how a 24h 38% spike maps to a bill delta.

If we give credits, finance wants a clear conversion trigger (commit increase or contract extension).

-Aditya

Alice — thanks for the data, and sorry for the surprise charge. We're proposing two pragmatic options so you can choose what fits FinAdvisor's runway:

Option A — Pilot auto-burst protection (short-term)
- 90-day pilot that enables a capped auto-burst buffer equal to 25% of committed throughput for short bursts (max burst duration 4 hours/day).
- Metering: buffer usage metered; billed monthly at committed rate + 15% surcharge.
- One-time onboarding credit: we will credit the first 24h of buffer usage (up to $5k) to help with the transition.

Option B — Commit uplift (recommended for sustained growth)
- Increase committed pool by 50% for 12 months; reduced committed price (15% discount on incremental commit).
- Immediate invoice credit: we will apply a pro-rated credit equal to 12 hours of above-commit consumption if they sign within 14 days.

Both options preserve their ability to set hard throttles or route to hosted fallback. If you want, we can model the two options against the attached spike_report_q3.csv and show the expected monthly bill delta.

Next step: propose a quick 30m call Wed 14:00 PT to walk through numbers and paperwork.

Best,
